headline: High: Langflow’s unsandboxed server-side execution and shared state can leak or corrupt data when paired with Rasa’s allowlisted external messaging integrations.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Langflow can chain multiple agents and exposes files and arbitrary HTTP services; Rasa ingests text/voice from messaging channels. If Langflow outputs are routed into Rasa flows, attacker-controlled content can cross the boundary and be treated as instructions. The pair lacks documented provenance tracking or isolation in the profiles, so the interaction is plausible but not proven.
conditions: IF Langflow flow outputs are forwarded into Rasa message handlers without provenance tags
IF Rasa templates or actions parse Langflow-generated text as instructions
mitigations: Add a provenance prefix to all Langflow outputs before handoff
Insert a human review step for any Langflow-to-Rasa instruction text
Restrict Rasa handlers to a fixed schema for upstream content
requires-engineering: implement content-signing between the two systems

B_data_leakage.rationale: Langflow reads and writes the server filesystem and stores per-flow credentials, while Rasa handles text/voice and can send traffic through allowlisted channels. If both are deployed against the same workspace or shared secrets, sensitive flow inputs can reach Rasa outputs or external messaging surfaces. The profiles show a plausible shared-data path, but not a direct documented leak.
conditions: IF both agents are deployed on the same host or workspace
IF Langflow flow inputs include secrets or sensitive documents
IF Rasa responses or channel integrations echo upstream content externally
mitigations: Separate the agents onto distinct workspaces
Move secrets out of Langflow flow storage
Disable echoing of upstream content in Rasa responses
Review allowlisted outbound channels for sensitive payloads
requires-engineering: add DLP filtering at the handoff boundary

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Langflow has broad filesystem write, shell, subprocess, and broad network egress; Rasa has allowlisted network egress and multiple messaging integrations. Their capabilities overlap on mutable external resources and outbound channels, so concurrent use can conflict or race on shared services. The profiles do not show locking or coordination, so uncertainty pushes this to medium.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same filesystem or deployment directory
IF both agents call the same external API or messaging endpoint
IF no orchestrator-level lock serializes their writes
mitigations: Assign separate directories and credentials
Serialize writes through a single orchestrator
Limit Langflow egress to required endpoints only
Restrict Rasa to non-overlapping channels
requires-engineering: add resource locking for shared mutable targets

D_cascading_error.rationale: Langflow can chain multiple agents and run unsandboxed Python code server-side, so its outputs may be treated as authoritative workflow inputs. Rasa is a customer-support bot that can act on dialogue and send messages through external channels. If Langflow-generated facts feed Rasa without verification, errors can cascade into user-facing actions or incorrect support responses.
conditions: IF Langflow output is used as a source of truth for Rasa dialogue policy or responses
IF no verification step checks Langflow-produced facts before Rasa sends messages
mitigations: Require Rasa to verify all Langflow facts against a second source
Add a confidence threshold before any user-facing response
Route Langflow outputs to a draft queue only
Log and review mismatches between the two systems
requires-engineering: build a validation layer between agents

E_compliance.rationale: Langflow stores per-flow credentials and processes flow inputs on a server filesystem, while Rasa handles text and voice through external messaging channels. If regulated or personal data enters Langflow and is then surfaced by Rasa, retention and residency obligations can diverge. The profiles do not document matching compliance controls, so the safer choice is medium.
conditions: IF regulated personal data is processed in Langflow flows
IF Rasa channels retain transcripts or metadata longer than Langflow
IF the deployment spans jurisdictions with different residency rules
mitigations: Minimize regulated data in both systems
Set explicit retention limits on transcripts and flow logs
Document data residency for each channel
Review whether any channel is out of scope for the data class
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for retention and residency
